title: Apex Predator
description: The Apex Predator, commonly known as the Duck, is a Level 1 Monster in R.E.P.O. and acts as a seemingly innocent creature until the player tries to touch it.

sections.text: Becomes Enraged and Dangerous when grabbed or hurt
The Apex Predator, commonly known as the Duck, is a Level 1 Monster in R.E.P.O. and acts as a seemingly innocent creature until the player tries to touch it.
The Apex Predator resembles a small duckling with wide adorable eyes and a round cute body. It stays this way until it is pet.
Once pet it becomes enraged. It retains the general shape but it flies with a comically wide beak with horrific sharp teeth. The cute eyes are barely visible in the enraged form.

Upon spotting a player, the Apex Predator will follow them, constantly trying to stay on their crosshair position to bait the player to grab it. If the player looks up or jumps, the duck will jump as well to maintain visibility.

If grabbed or damaged by anything, the Apex Predator will become enraged and grow a large, toothy maw before immediately chasing the player who angered it (or the closest player if damaged indirectly). It will be aggressive for ten seconds and begin rapidly biting, dealing damage up to three times per second. It can follow players underneath or above objects, such as tables. Once it begins its pursuit, it will always know the location of the player it's targeting. Hiding is impossible, so outrunning it is the only option.
If the Apex Predator falls into a pit, it will fly back up unless stunned. It can continuously fly for 30 seconds, and will exhaust itself and fall to its death after the 30 seconds are up.

Luring the Apex Predator into a toilet (and flushing) or a Swiftbroom cauldron will launch and stun it for ~14 seconds. It can be slammed to death while stunned.
Note that the Museum does have security lasers, but these are not necessarily assured to kill it. They do not keep it stunned for very long or do enough damage for it to be a feasible tech.

It’s possible to stun the Apex Predator by tumble launching into it, dealing 15 damage. It will usually get pushed back far and fast, usually taking additional Physics damage. However, this is difficult to pull off due to its small size and airborne movement.
It will become aggressive to the closest player within 10 units around it. If no players are around that area, it will get back up and do nothing.

The Apex Predator can be crushed by an extraction point for an easy kill. It will remain largely stationary at the location of the players cursor. This, conveniently, also gives the player the money from its Enemy Valuable if the duck is far enough into extraction. But if it is too close to the edge, the valuable will remain as an item instead of being sold and can be sold at the next extraction.

The Apex Predator loses interest quickly. Running into the next room and hiding under something is often enough for it to stop pursuing the player.  
However, since the Apex Predator follows the player's cursor, looking at a wall with an adjacent room behind it to guide it into that room and break line of sight. After a few seconds, it will lose track of the player.

Since the Apex Predator cannot fly forever, players can attempt to push it into a pit then block it above with any big item, like a C.A.R.T., until it falls.

Even in its enraged state, the Apex Predator can still be stunned and/or killed. A carefully aimed attack will disrupt its aggression, although it will enrage again once it recovers from the stun unless killed.

It is impossible to lift the duck, as the player would require 833,328 Strength Upgrades to achieve 999,999 force required. Even debug editing, the maximum is less than 100, preventing this from being achievable.
With mods, it is possible to lift the duck; if done, the player will get the same result as when they pick up any other monster, except that it will stay docile.

A painting in the Museum of Human Art shows what appears to be Dumgolf using his staff on a duck, implying that the duck's mutations are a byproduct of a spell.
Another painting in the Museum depicts the Apex Predator in Cubism, implying that monsters were known about prior to the Incident that left the world in the current state.
The Apex Predator's damage per second is the same as Reaper's being 10 damage every ~0.2 seconds.
